note: Each source is pinned to the commit whose licence was read, and the licence was read from that commit rather than from the default branch. A refused source contributed no bytes. The repository's own text is the one source copied off disk rather than fetched at a pinned SHA: its entry records the revision it was read at, whether the working tree matched that revision (`clean`) and a digest over the path and content of every file copied (`treeDigest`), because a copy of a dirty tree is a record of what was read rather than a recipe that can be replayed from the commit it names.
purpose: The licence-checked public sources an assembled corpus is built from.

sources.why: This repository's own text: the one corpus source whose right to be trained on is not in question.
A small, readable application framework: BSD-3-Clause, and small enough to be read in full.
A second language and a second licence shape (MIT), so the corpus is not one project's idiom.
Apache-2.0 is the licence the composed path would have allowed; the corpus allowlist is the same list, so the two paths agree about what may be used.

A second language at real scale. The cap was 4 MB while the corpus was 13.65 MB; a subword corpus needs orders of magnitude more text than that, so it is raised rather than kept as a souvenir of the smaller run.
MIT again, and test code: a different register from library code, which is most of what the other sources contribute.
Documentation-heavy Python: mostly prose, which balances source code in the corpus.
The largest Apache-2.0 Go codebase in wide use, and its API reference is configuration documentation rather than prose about a library.
A second large BSD-3-Clause project, with Cython as well as Python, so the corpus is not one authoring style.
Documentation-heavy numeric Python; its user guide is long-form explanation rather than API listing.
A large MIT TypeScript application: event-driven, message-passing code, which is structurally different from library code.
MIT, and front-end code with a documentation site in the same repository.
A second TypeScript application of a different shape from vscode's, under MIT rather than Apache-2.0.
A compiler rather than an application: code that generates code, which the corpus had none of.
PHP: a language the corpus would otherwise have none of, and one whose idioms differ sharply from the rest.
A taught curriculum: notebooks mix explanation with code, which is closer to the register of an assistant than any other source here.
The largest BSD-3-Clause teaching corpus: instructional English in `blockquote` and challenge text, which is natural language rather than API reference.
